translation: When all three regions are firm (lao) and run straight up and down, it is the Chong vessel; it causes cold hernia in the chest. The Pulse Classic says: When the pulse comes with the center solid and firm, reaching straight to the guan, it is the Chong vessel; when it moves it causes lower abdominal pain rushing upward to the heart, with abdominal masses, hernia, and enuresis, and in women loss of pregnancy. When the front region bounces left and right, it is the Yang Heel (qiao) vessel; when it moves it causes lower back and spine pain, mania-epilepsy with falling and sheep-like bleating, hemiplegia, bi with numbness, and stiffness of the body.
